analysis.title: Rates Spark: ECB reserve rethink would bring funding pressure closer
key_insights: The ECB looks closer to raising the minimum reserve requirement (MRR) for banks than previously thought. Per a Reuters report cited by ING, the ECB will discuss the move next week and decide at its December meeting, with a majority of board members said to be supportive.

Doubling the MRR from 1% to 2% of the deposit and short-term liability base would save the ECB €4.4bn a year at current rates. ING sees this as the primary motivation, since it reduces the cost of past bond-buying programmes.
Doubling the MRR would cut excess reserves by €175bn from the current €2.1tr. That level is already moving into a range where the ECB had previously estimated reserves would no longer be 'abundant'.
Short-term funding rates would be closer to the point where they feel upward pressure. Some banks might find ECB liquidity operations more appealing as a result.

ING thinks the ECB's earlier reasoning against the change should still hold: the MRR is a blunt tool with uneven impact because excess reserves are not evenly distributed. The ECB may be encouraged by short-term funding markets, including cross-border, running smoothly.
To limit disruption, the ECB could pair an MRR increase with an announcement of structural (longer-term) liquidity operations, which are part of the new operational framework.

US dynamics are driving rates. The Treasury curve flattened as the front end came under pressure from hawkish Fed comments and FOMC minutes. A couple of Fed officials hinted that a hike of more than 25bp in December could be appropriate.

Longer Treasury yields are sensitive to weak equity markets and jittery tech sentiment. Solid Nvidia earnings did not lift the overall gloom, and 10y US Treasury yields are testing their way back to 5.05%.

European rates are more range-bound with fewer domestic drivers. ECB commentary leans hawkish: Vujcic said price pressures beyond energy would emerge 'for sure' next year and did not rule out more hikes after a likely one in December.
earnings_insights: Nvidia reported solid earnings (reported, per ING's comment) but the result was not enough to lift weakness in equity markets. No figures given.
